entities.name: Muhammad ibn Buzurg-Ummid
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Muhammad ibn Buzurg-Ummid was the third ruler of the Nizari Ismailis, succeeding his father Kiyā Buzurg-Ummīd and preceding his son Hassan ibn Hassan. He was the son of Kiyā Buzurg-Ummīd and ruled from 1138 to 1162. His rule was marked by the expansion of the Ismaili network and the construction of new fortresses, including the fortress of Rudbar. The Nizari Ismailis, under Muhammad ibn Buzurg-Ummid's leadership, faced persecution from the Seljuk Turks and the Sunni Muslim world, leading to a significant increase in Ismaili numbers in the region. The Ismaili community in Alamut, the fortress city in which Muhammad ibn Buzurg-Ummid resided, was a major center of learning and scholarship, attracting scholars and intellectuals from across the Islamic world. Despite his efforts to promote Ismaili teachings, Muhammad ibn Buzurg-Ummid's rule was ultimately cut short by his death in 1162, at the age of 24. His legacy, however, continued to shape the course of Ismaili history, inspiring his successor, Hassan ibn Hassan, to continue the expansion of the Ismaili network and the promotion of Ismaili teachings.
